To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

RL agents with limited information processing resources (e.g., limited memory) are more robust to changes in the environment than agents with unlimited resources, and that the RL problem of optimizing utility within capacity-limits can be mapped to the problem of rate-distortion theory.

1) the problem of optimizing utility within capacity-limits is equivalent to a rate-distortion problem; 2) we develop an RL algorithm that optimizes a rate-distortion tradeoff; 3) the algorithm achieves faster and better learning in a gridworld environment compared to the tabular actor-critc algorithm; 4) agents with capacity-limits exhibit superior transfer to new environments, and are less prone to 'overfitting', compared to agents with unlimited capacity.
RL agents that are limited in their ability to represent a policy are better able to learn a behavioral strategy that is robust to changes in the environment.
